items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: Gary Foster, who’s been a good friend of mine for many years

ctx.x: You know I think historians and sociologists and so forth who write about the music, they want it to be an issue more than it is. Because it’s better copy.

Oh yeah. And in relation to jazz education, one of the things that I deal with even with jazz majors let alone with people that are not musicians or that don’t play jazz, is they still want to believe this myth that certain people are just anointed from above or that if you just ingest the right substance or hang out with the masters, you know, that this stuff is going to rub off. And they even sometimes fall prey to these myths because it’s a more attractive story. It’s the more fun thing to believe. It just…
I think I just saw it recently. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
